tasks.gr9-lithosphere-earth-resources-t4: Topic: Lithosphere and Earth Resources. Cover rocks, minerals, Earth structure, plate tectonics, mining, fossil fuels, and renewable resources. Ask learners to classify rock types, explain plate movement, evaluate mining impacts, or compare renewable and non-renewable resources.
tasks.gr9-stars-universe-t4: Topic: Stars and the Universe. Cover stars as fusion reactors, star life cycles (nebula to death), galaxies, the Milky Way, and the scale of the universe. Ask learners to sequence star life stages, explain nuclear fusion, describe galaxy organisation, or interpret the vast distances in space.
tasks.gr9-atmosphere-t4: Topic: The Atmosphere (Grade 9 Natural Sciences, Term 4). Cover the atmosphere as the mixture of gases held around the Earth by gravity (air: nitrogen 78%, oxygen 21%, carbon dioxide less than 1%, other gases including water vapour about 1%), density decreasing with height, the four layers (troposphere from sea level to about 10 km with more than 70% of the mass, all weather and all life; stratosphere about 10 to 50 km with the band of ozone that absorbs ultraviolet radiation so it warms with height; mesosphere about 50 to 80 km, extremely thin and cold, burns up small rocks; thermosphere above 80 km, the ISS at about 370 km), temperature gradient in the troposphere of about 1 degree Celsius per 100 m in still air (always give the sea-level temperature), scale drawings of the layers, the greenhouse effect as natural (greenhouse gases carbon dioxide, water vapour and methane trap heat), global warming and its effects (climate change, rising sea levels, food shortages, mass extinctions). Teach that greenhouse gases trap heat; do not ask which kind of radiation is trapped. Describe any situation in words and numbers (there is no picture). Ask Grade 9 learners to identify, explain and calculate.
